## Security verdict: PASS WITH NOTES

PR #165, exact head `46712bbe95cadc6b10d38cae6e8871e4c70fedc6`.

All four changed files were reviewed. No high-confidence new security vulnerability was identified. The added arguments remove the modal question tools without replacing the launcher's existing settings or permission arguments.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| - | - | - | - | No new vulnerability identified | - |

### Launch-control evidence

- `crates/harnesses/src/spawn.rs:190-209` adds Copilot `--no-ask-user` alongside the existing `--yolo`. Model, context, effort handling and configuration inputs are unchanged. This build's CLI documentation defines the flag as disabling the question-form tool, not changing other permission settings; asking in ordinary replies remains possible.
- `spawn.rs:178-188` adds the discrete pair `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion` for Claude. Existing `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and conditional `--settings {"crossSessionInbound":"accept"}` remain separate, unchanged arguments. No earlier generated `--disallowedTools` option is replaced. The official Claude CLI reference describes a bare tool name as removing that matching tool from context.
- `crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:1471-1548` uses the shared builder/wrapper path. Revive preserves the previous inbound setting and uses that same launcher (`crates/daemon/src/http/revive.rs:423-441`). The executor passes discrete arguments through `ProcessCommand`, without shell interpretation (`crates/cli/src/main.rs:3813-3830`).
- Test source `crates/harnesses/src/spawn.rs:408-544` covers both harnesses with and without resume, pins fresh-launch argv, and retains the exact settings assertion.

The inherited broad permission arguments are not introduced or broadened by this PR. This is tool-surface suppression, not a new permission boundary. The unchanged TS control builder is not used by the inspected runtime launch path; full launch-path correctness is separately reviewer-owned.

### Privacy and proof

The changed spawn API paragraph (`docs/how/pij-rs-api.md:137`), quoted Copilot argv (`docs/how/copilot-native-extension.md:86`) and D-F110-1 (`docs/difficulties.md:123`) add no identified secret or private machine path under C19/C21.

GitHub metadata and the independent remote pull ref agree on the full reviewed SHA; GitHub reports CLEAN. CI run `42411875834` and Delivers run `42411875819` both identify that SHA and success.

The reported installed-CLI and matching-wrapper canaries are supporting operator evidence, not independently repeated here. Source and pinned argv establish preservation of the generated arguments; merge precedence with arbitrary inherited external Claude deny-rule configuration was not independently exercised. No local builds, tests, probes, credential reads or launch/canary execution were performed.

References for flag semantics: this Copilot CLI build's `--no-ask-user` / `--yolo` documentation, and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference (`--disallowedTools`).
